hero.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway in Martin County after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
hero.body:
Demolition began this week at Murray Middle School in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized. The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay.

Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete. Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, explained that the school was already scheduled for significant improvements before the hurricane struck. "Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab," said Gernaine. "With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine we were able to add these on."

The tornadoes destroyed buildings 18, 10, and nine located in the back of the campus. The district was able to incorporate reconstruction of those buildings into the planned improvements that were already scheduled. This allowed the school to address both the planned upgrades and the tornado damage in a single comprehensive project. The Martin County School District hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027.

The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out of the construction area. The safety measures are designed to separate the active construction site from areas where students attend classes and move around campus. While the demolition and reconstruction work continues, school operations will proceed with displaced students using portable classrooms as temporary learning spaces until the new permanent structures are completed.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds, David Jolly lead Florida governor's race as primary nears
cards.body:
Republican U.S. Representative Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly have emerged as frontrunners in Florida's governor's race as the July 18 primary approaches. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48 percent, followed by Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins at 9 percent, businessman James Fishback at 8 percent and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 4 percent. About 26 percent of respondents remained undecided. Donalds holds a major financial advantage, with his campaign announcing more than $90 million raised across his campaign operation. President Donald Trump has endorsed Donalds, while Governor Ron DeSantis, who appointed Collins lieutenant governor in August 2025, has remained publicly neutral in the primary. A June Change Research survey commissioned by Freedom Project USA showed Jolly leading Donalds 47 percent to 42 percent among registered voters and 49 percent to 43 percent among likely voters, though respondents were shown prepared descriptions of both candidates before being asked whom they supported.

Collins is challenging Fishback's eligibility, alleging Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., and does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida, has lived in the state throughout his life and purchased a Washington condo only to visit his parents. The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Senator Ted Cruz, announced a $400,000 campaign targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. Jolly moved this week to address his past business and political relationship with Clearwater financier Leo Govoni. Federal prosecutors allege Govoni and accountant John Witeck stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit that managed trust funds for people with disabilities and other special needs. The indictment alleges the scheme operated from 2009 through 2025. Jolly previously worked as a vice president at Boston Finance Group, a Govoni-controlled company, before entering Congress. Jolly is not a defendant in the case.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff ramps up traffic enforcement with deputies targeting speeders on Midway Road, U.S. 1
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is intensifying traffic enforcement this summer, deploying additional deputies and launching a new targeting initiative aimed at reducing speeding and reckless driving across the county. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said traffic is the top concern among residents and described the crackdown as a quality of life issue. Del Toro is using extra deputies from the sheriff's school resource division to boost enforcement while the school year is on break and is placing top-performing deputies in areas of concern.

Deputies Christopher Rodrigues and Cheyenne Benning are among those targeting high-problem corridors, including Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive. Benning said the county sees a lot of excessive speeding and that most recently she had someone pass her on I-95 doing 105 mph. Rodrigues said he stopped a driver doing 72 mph on Midway Road and another doing 98 mph on U.S. 1. On Indian River Drive, where the speed limit is 25 mph, Rodrigues said his top recorded speed was 73 mph.

In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. The enforcement push is part of a broader strategy Del Toro put in place when he took office. He eliminated the agency's dedicated traffic unit and made traffic enforcement the responsibility of every deputy. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, a 155% increase.

Local drivers described what they see on county roads as serious problems. Ashley, a St. Lucie County resident, said the situation is insane and that nobody slows down. Jessica, another local driver, said drivers are careless and cut others off. Del Toro said he has a family that drives on these roadways and cares about his loved ones and everyone else's loved ones. He said he wants to make this a safer community.

cards.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to New York JFK flights after nine months, citing low demand
cards.body:
JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airline announced that service between the two airports will end Sept. 9, just nine months after the route began operating with much fanfare and optimistic passengers. JetBlue will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route, and all affected customers will be notified directly by the airline and will receive full refunds.

"Demand for this new route has not materialized as we had hoped," JetBlue said in a statement to WPTV. The decision marks a setback for Vero Beach Regional Airport's efforts to expand commercial service in recent years. The JFK route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area.

The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a game changer for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast. However, those hopes did not translate into sustained passenger numbers sufficient to keep the route viable. While JetBlue's Boston route continues to serve travelers seeking alternatives to larger South Florida airports, the loss of the JFK connection removes what had been viewed as a significant transportation option for the region.

JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The cancellation serves as a reminder that new airline routes, even those launched with considerable excitement and perceived demand, require sustained passenger support to remain economically viable for carriers.

cards.headline: JetBlue ending direct flights from Vero Beach to New York JFK after nine months, citing low demand
cards.body:
JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airline announced that service between the two airports will end Sept. 9, just nine months after the route began operating with much fanfare and optimistic passengers. JetBlue told WPTV that demand for this new route has not materialized as the airline had hoped. The carrier will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route, and all affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

The JFK-Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area. The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a game changer for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast. The route's cancellation comes as a disappointment less than a year after its debut, when local officials and travelers celebrated the expanded connectivity for the region.

Vero Beach Regional Airport has worked to expand its commercial service in recent years, with JetBlue's Boston route continuing to serve travelers seeking alternatives to larger South Florida airports. The airport's efforts to attract more direct flights have aimed to provide residents and visitors with more convenient travel options without the need to drive to airports in Fort Lauderdale, West Palm Beach, or Orlando. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service.

Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The airline will notify all affected customers about the cancellation and provide full refunds for those who cannot or do not wish to rebook on alternative flights. The decision to end the JFK route reflects the challenges smaller regional airports face in sustaining commercial air service, even when serving potentially attractive markets. While the Boston route remains in operation, the loss of direct JFK service eliminates what many had hoped would be a permanent connection between the Treasure Coast and the New York metropolitan area.

cards.headline: Humane Society of the Treasure Coast seeks foster, adoption help during shelter renovation
cards.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation that has affected about 67 animals on site.
cards.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation. The construction will modernize the shelter, improve animal living spaces, enhance adoption areas, and create more comfortable and visible spaces to care for animals. In the meantime, the renovation presents significant challenges for the animals, who are being held in smaller spaces during the work.

Sarah Fisher of the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast said the animals are really being affected by the sound of the construction. It's very, very loud and the sound being in a closed kennel can be very stressful for an animal. About 50 animals are currently in foster care, but the shelter is hoping to get the remaining 67 animals housed on-site either fostered or adopted, with most of them being dogs. The shelter continues to receive animals daily and is on a mission to get them out as quickly as they come in.

cards.headline: Villa Del Sol residents in St. Lucie County return home after nearly two years of displacement
cards.teaser: Villa Del Sol residents in St. Lucie County are able to return home after nearly two years of being displaced from their condos due to structural damage. Some residents who cannot afford to return are filing for bankruptcy and foreclosure.
cards.body:
Villa Del Sol residents in St. Lucie County told WPTV they are able to return home after nearly two years of being displaced from their condos. Residents said they were notified last month they could return to their condos, after an inspection in August 2024 found structural damage in buildings 3, 4, and 5, which were deemed unsafe. Katie Johnson was the first to share to WPTV that residents had been told they could come back. WPTV received emails sent to residents from the Board of Directors telling them they could return. WPTV also obtained a letter from engineers sent to St. Lucie County's Building Department requesting they lift occupancy restrictions following their special inspection. Katie Johnson described the work still underway at the property, saying they are still moving the dirt back under the buildings. Robert Segedin took WPTV inside his family's home, excited to return but thinking about those who cannot.

Eric Johnson is among those not coming back. He was one of the first residents WPTV met at Villa Del Sol and is now living in Georgia. Eric said the financial toll has been severe, saying he and his family had to drain out all their savings accounts and all their 401ks just trying to make ends meet while this was going on. He is filing for bankruptcy and filing his condo for foreclosure. Katie Johnson said she is thinking of neighbors like Eric Johnson who cannot return, saying she feels so bad that some were hit harder than others with the situation.

cards.headline: Security First Insurance lowers homeowners rates 5.6% for Florida customers
cards.teaser: Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years.
cards.body:
Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years. Melissa Burt DeVriese, president of Security First, said customers are seeing the impact of the rate decreases. Insurance companies have been reducing rates or holding them stable as more companies cite a reduction in lawsuits from state reforms. Burt DeVriese said all those savings the company is required to pass along to customers, and they have been.

Security First also announced new discounts and a disappearing deductible that rewards claims-free customers by reducing their deductible over time. Over the course of five years, the deductible goes down 20 percent each year as long as customers do not have a loss. Once a customer has a loss, the discounted deductible applies, and then it resets back to the full deductible amount. Based in Ormond Beach, Security First has about 155,000 policies in the state. Burt DeVriese said Security First is committed to writing more policies in southeast Florida. Online firm Insurify reports that in 2026 Florida homeowners pay the highest average premium in the country at $8,292. State insurance regulators said that with more companies and more competition, homeowners should seek better premiums by shopping around.

hero.headline: Flip City Gym and Cheer gymnasts finish top 15 at nationals, qualify for Junior Olympics
hero.body:
Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer earned a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine competed as a team after advancing through local competitions, states, and regionals during what Head Coach Candice Lazuka described as a strong season.

The team came close to a perfect score at the national competition. Lazuka said the gymnasts scored a 9.9, approaching the rare perfect 10. The finish qualified the team for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Lazuka noted the trio competed locally and traveled before advancing to states and regionals during what she called a strong season for the program.

Each gymnast found her way to the sport through a different path. Rose-Daris said it started with a simple skill. "It wasn't really gymnastics, it was the fact that I knew how to do a cartwheel," Rose-Daris said. Supan drew inspiration from watching elite athletes perform. "All the gymnasts that I saw on YouTube, and how amazing they are, and how fun it looks," Supan said. Rine said the appeal lies in continuous growth. "I love it because I learn new things," Rine said.

The gymnasts expressed excitement about competing at the Junior Olympics next month. Rine has a specific target heading into the competition. "Getting first place on floors," Rine said. Rose-Daris emphasized the travel opportunity the competition presents. "It's going to be really fun that I'm going to an entire different part of the world," Rose-Daris said. Supan described her feelings about the upcoming event simply. "It's happy and exciting at the same time," Supan said. The team will represent Flip City Gym and Cheer in Iowa as they compete against other top qualifiers from across the country.

cards.headline: Argentina rallies past England with late goals to reach World Cup final
cards.teaser: Defending World Cup champion Argentina scored twice in the final minutes to defeat England 2-1 and advance to Sunday's final against Spain.
cards.body:
Trailing 1-0 going into the 85th minute, Argentina rallied for a 2-1 victory over England on Wednesday with goals from Enzo Fernandez and substitute Lautaro Martinez to advance to the World Cup final. Anthony Gordon scored the opening goal for England in the 55th minute. Messi fed the ball to Fernandez to sweep in the equalizer from outside the box in the 85th minute, and two minutes into stoppage time, Messi sent in a cross for Martinez to head in the winner. Martinez said he told Alexis Mac Allister that he was going to come on and win it. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves while Mac Allister sent a header off the post as Argentina mounted wave after wave of attacks.

The defending champions will take on European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. England captain Harry Kane said he was gutted for the team, staff and fans, saying the players gave every bit of blood, sweat and tears. England coach Thomas Tuchel said his substitutions seemed more intent on holding on rather than killing the game off with another goal. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the team showed collectiveness, brotherhood and fight to the very end. England came up short in the World Cup semifinals for the third time after losses to Germany in 1990 and Croatia in 2018.

cards.headline: World Cup final four set after quarterfinal matches
cards.teaser: England, Argentina, Spain, and France advanced to the World Cup semifinals after weekend and Monday quarterfinal matches.
cards.body:
England and Argentina advanced to the semifinals after two quarterfinals over the weekend against Norway and Switzerland. For England, Jude Bellingham netted twice to inspire his team past Erling Haaland's Norway. Argentina needed Julián Alvarez's goal in extra time to help the team advance past Switzerland with a controversial VAR call. The last four is now complete with the four highest-ranked teams reaching the semifinals. Both Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham have scored six goals in the competition for England. Argentina has scored the most goals out of anyone in the competition with 17.

England was last in a World Cup semifinal in 2018 but lost on that occasion to Croatia. With the country looking for its first World Cup title since 1966, there is immense pressure on Kane and Bellingham to keep producing match-winning moments. Argentina has the added bonus of experience, with many members of the current squad winning the title back in 2022. Lionel Messi has scored and provided crucial assists for Argentina as the defending champion looks to repeat. France faces Spain in the other semifinal, with France considered by many to be the tournament favorite. Spain beat France in the semifinals of Euro 2024 and also defeated France in the Nations League last year.

hero.headline: Palm Beach County Food Bank serves 2,500 hot meals daily to local children this summer
hero.teaser: The Palm Beach County Food Bank in Lake Worth Beach supports more than 35 Summer BreakSpot sites across the county, serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children while school is out.
hero.body:
The Palm Beach County Food Bank in Lake Worth Beach is helping provide thousands of free meals to children this summer through Florida's Summer BreakSpot program, according to Food Bank leaders. The nonprofit organization said it supports more than 35 Summer BreakSpot sites across Palm Beach County, serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children while school is out for the summer. According to the Palm Beach County Food Bank, the organization prepared more than 36,000 hot meals in June alone.

During a live Shining A Light broadcast on WPTV, Palm Beach County Food Bank CEO Jamie Kendall and Culinary Director Chef Doug Barg gave viewers a behind-the-scenes look inside the Michelle Hagerty Community Kitchen, where meals are prepared and loaded onto trucks for early morning deliveries across the county. Chef Doug Barg walked viewers through the food production process, showing how culinary teams prepare, package and organize meals before they are loaded onto delivery trucks. The loading dock operation featured drivers and volunteers preparing for morning deliveries to Summer BreakSpot sites throughout Palm Beach County. The Palm Beach County Food Bank said volunteers and community support are critical to maintaining the program during the busy summer season. The Palm Beach County Food Bank is located at 701 Boutwell Road, Suite A-1, in Lake Worth Beach.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Zoo extends Kids Free promotion through August 10
cards.teaser: Palm Beach Zoo's popular Kids Free promotion has been extended through Aug. 10. Under the program, up to four children ages 3 to 12 receive free admission with the purchase of one adult ticket.
cards.body:
Palm Beach Zoo's popular Kids Free promotion has been extended through Aug. 10, according to zoo officials. Under the program, up to four children ages 3 to 12 receive free admission with the purchase of one adult ticket. Amanda Joiner, the zoo's chief marketing and technology officer, said the extension is designed to help local families enjoy affordable outings during the hottest stretch of summer while still supporting the zoo's conservation mission.

The zoo's newest koala joey is officially a boy and now has a name: Bonza. That's Aussie slang for awesome or excellent, Joiner said. Zoo staff members from departments ranging from accounting to marketing helped document and share the koala family's journey with the public.

Palm Beach Zoo also announced the return of its Wild Night Out series, an adults-only after-hours experience happening on the last Saturdays of July, August and September. The themed nights include Paws & Santa Claus in July, Tails & Touchdowns in August and Decades After Dark in September. Palm Beach Zoo is located at 1301 Summit Blvd.

hero.headline: Security First Insurance cuts Florida homeowner rates 5.6 percent
hero.teaser: The Ormond Beach-based insurer announced the rate reduction Thursday, the latest in a series of decreases over the last two years.
hero.body:
Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6 percent, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years. Insurance companies have been reducing rates or holding them stable as more companies cite a reduction in lawsuits from state reforms. Melissa Burt DeVriese, president of Security First, said the company is required to pass savings along to customers. "All those savings we're required to pass along to customers, and we have been," Burt DeVriese said.

Security First also announced new discounts and a disappearing deductible that rewards claims-free customers by reducing their deductible over time. The program lowers the deductible by 20 percent each year for policyholders who remain claims-free, continuing over a five-year period. "Over the course of five years, every year your deductible goes down 20 percent as long as you don't have a loss; once you have a loss, the discounted deductible applies, and then it resets back to the full deductible amount, so it rewards consumers who don't have losses," Burt DeVriese said. Once a customer files a claim, the reduced deductible applies to that claim, and then the deductible resets to its original full amount.

Based in Ormond Beach, Security First has about 155,000 policies in the state. The company is working to expand its customer base in parts of the state where insurance costs remain elevated. "Security First is committed to writing more policies in southeast Florida," Burt DeVriese said. The company's customers have been experiencing the benefits of the rate reductions the insurer has implemented. "Our customers are seeing the impact of our rate decreases," Burt DeVriese said.

Premiums in South Florida generally run high, and online firm Insurify reports that in 2026 Florida homeowners pay the highest average premium in the country at $8,292. State insurance regulators said that with more companies and more competition, homeowners should seek better premiums by shopping around. The recent trend of rate decreases and rate stability among Florida insurance companies reflects the effects of state reforms that have reduced lawsuit activity in the insurance sector.

cards.body:
Republican U.S. Representative Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly have emerged as frontrunners in Florida's governor's race as the July 18 primary approaches. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48 percent, followed by Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins at 9 percent, businessman James Fishback at 8 percent and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 4 percent. About 26 percent of respondents remained undecided. Donalds holds a major financial advantage, with his campaign announcing more than $90 million raised across his campaign operation. President Donald Trump has endorsed Donalds, while Governor Ron DeSantis, who appointed Collins lieutenant governor in August 2025, has remained publicly neutral in the primary. A June Change Research survey commissioned by Freedom Project USA showed Jolly leading Donalds 47 percent to 42 percent among registered voters and 49 percent to 43 percent among likely voters, though respondents were shown prepared descriptions of both candidates before being asked whom they supported.

Collins is challenging Fishback's eligibility, alleging Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., and does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida, has lived in the state throughout his life and purchased a Washington condo only to visit his parents. The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Senator Ted Cruz, announced a $400,000 campaign targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. Jolly moved this week to address his past business and political relationship with Clearwater financier Leo Govoni. Federal prosecutors allege Govoni and accountant John Witeck stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit that managed trust funds for people with disabilities and other special needs. The indictment alleges the scheme operated from 2009 through 2025. Jolly previously worked as a vice president at Boston Finance Group, a Govoni-controlled company, before entering Congress. Jolly is not a defendant in the case.

hero.headline: Palm City weather spotter with Navy background discusses forecasting evolution
hero.teaser: A Palm City WPTV Weather Spotter with a Navy background spoke with WPTV First Alert Weather Meteorologist James Wieland about how weather forecasting technology has transformed over the decades.
hero.body:
A Palm City WPTV Weather Spotter with a lifelong passion for meteorology spoke with WPTV First Alert Weather Meteorologist James Wieland about how weather forecasting has evolved over the decades. Brian Botley served in the Navy, where mapping the weather was part of his duties. His interest in weather began as a child in Oakland Park, where he moved in 1951. Botley said his father was always plotting the hurricanes, which sparked his interest. He went into the Navy and was selected to go to the Aerographer's Mate School in Lakehurst. His first job was plotting weather maps. Botley said there were some satellites starting in 1961 or 1962, but it wasn't the coverage they have now.

Wieland showed Botley the technology used in today's weather coverage, which is a far cry from the tools available during his Navy days, and walked him through how computer models and modern radar systems have transformed forecasting. Botley said joining WPTV's Weather Spotter program felt like a natural extension of something he was already doing on his own. He said he does this all the time just on his own and thought it may be fun because there are other people there.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Opens Registration for Free City University Program
hero.teaser:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes
hero.body:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes begin Wednesday, Aug. 12, and will be held from **5:30 to 8:30 p.m. in the Council Chambers at Port St. Lucie City Hall**, located at 121 SW Port St. Lucie Blvd.

Participants will learn about City departments, municipal services and the decision-making processes that shape the community. The program also gives residents opportunities to meet City staff, ask questions and gain a closer look at the work involved in operating one of Florida's largest cities.

Residents who complete the course will receive a certificate of completion and may also choose to become a City Ambassador, helping share information about City programs and services throughout the community.

City University is intended to encourage civic engagement while strengthening connections between residents and local government. Since the program began in 2016, more than 600 residents have participated.

**Enrollment is limited to 160 participants.**

Residents who are unable to attend the in-person classes can also access City U on Demand, which offers a more flexible way to learn about Port St. Lucie government and municipal operations.

hero.headline: JetBlue ending direct flights from Vero Beach to New York JFK after nine months, citing low demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airline announced that service between the two airports will end Sept. 9, just nine months after the route began operating with much fanfare and optimistic passengers. JetBlue told WPTV that demand for this new route has not materialized as the airline had hoped. The carrier will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route, and all affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

The JFK-Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area. The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a game changer for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast. The route's cancellation comes as a disappointment less than a year after its debut, when local officials and travelers celebrated the expanded connectivity for the region.

Vero Beach Regional Airport has worked to expand its commercial service in recent years, with JetBlue's Boston route continuing to serve travelers seeking alternatives to larger South Florida airports. The airport's efforts to attract more direct flights have aimed to provide residents and visitors with more convenient travel options without the need to drive to airports in Fort Lauderdale, West Palm Beach, or Orlando. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service.

Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The airline will notify all affected customers about the cancellation and provide full refunds for those who cannot or do not wish to rebook on alternative flights. The decision to end the JFK route reflects the challenges smaller regional airports face in sustaining commercial air service, even when serving potentially attractive markets. While the Boston route remains in operation, the loss of direct JFK service eliminates what many had hoped would be a permanent connection between the Treasure Coast and the New York metropolitan area.
